title: How to do curls (strict barbell curls tutorial)
summary: A tutorial on strict EZ-bar curls. NH says to keep the elbows pinned to the sides with only a small finishing movement at the top, to avoid hip drive and raising the elbows (which turns the curl into a compound movement), and to stop around 45 degrees short of full extension to spare the biceps tendon. He applies the same angle logic to preacher curls.
claims: The curl has a low technical rating but is easy to mess up; the goal is to isolate the biceps and keep other muscles' involvement to a minimum, since true isolation does not exist
Turning the curl into a compound movement means you are always cheating
The EZ bar mainly affects wrist comfort and forearm engagement, not biceps activation
Grip width claims (close for short head, wide for long head) should be tested by experiment, not taken as a recipe
To activate the biceps, keep the elbows tucked at your sides without flaring or raising them; a slight elbow movement only to finish the top is fine
Raising the elbows forward makes it a power curl or front-raise curl that brings in a lot of shoulder
The recent strict-curl competition craze turned the curl into a strength contest where people raise the elbows, which helps strength but not biceps growth
Lifting more weight does not automatically mean bigger arms if the extra weight is moved by other muscles
People who cite shoulder flexion as part of the curl misread the data: only the small motion at the top is needed; any more and you drift into cheating
Bringing the elbows up and back down involves nearly every upper-body joint, turning the curl into a full compound movement
The two levels of curl cheating are raising the elbows and hip-driving from the bottom, which is essentially a supinated clean
Dumbbells make cheating harder than the EZ bar
Using the hips to bounce the bar does nothing for the biceps; done strictly, you get both the positive and the negative
Any time people compete on a lift they bastardise it; strict-curl competitions are really cheat competitions once the elbows leave the sides
Curling with your back against a wall is easier because you can push the elbows into it; a true strict curl is standing free with no hip flexion and no elbow raise
Do not fully extend the arm at the bottom of a curl; stop around 45 degrees to keep tension and avoid using the tendon's elasticity
On the preacher curl the elbow sits further forward, so judge the 45 degree limit by the angle between upper arm and shoulder, and do not let the shoulder follow the bar down
Going below that range over-involves the biceps tendon and only creates tendinitis without helping gains
Without a preacher bench, raise the elbows and set them close to the chest with a narrower grip to be your own preacher
exercises: elbows pinned to sides; small finishing elbow motion only; no hip drive; standing free, not against wall; stop ~45 deg short of lockout
maximises biceps involvement and spares the tendon
involves shoulders and other joints; for strength, not biceps growth
stop at 45 deg of shoulder-arm angle; shoulder stays put
narrower grip; elbows raised close to chest; 45 deg range
